correctness.rationale: For all real fractional committees, the threshold exchange lemma excludes a positive measure of thresholds with more selected removals than additions in any PO committee. Exact seat conservation then forces almost every threshold to be size preserving, and strict fractional dominance integrates to a strict integral dominance at some such threshold. The three-approval counterexample is checked against all ten integral committees and exact fractional utilities; all 1024 degree-two support patterns on four candidates were independently exercised on rational grids without counterexample. The finite grid is supporting evidence only.

value.rationale: This gives an unrestricted all-size positive class for fractional robustness in committee choice, with the natural first nontrivial ballot-sparsity threshold. The degree-two class is outside the previously applied single-dominance-only framework, so its structural argument identifies a genuinely different mechanism. The sharp size-three failure supplies a meaningful boundary, although general PO/fPO separation was already known.
